requirement:
In authored book chapters, a passage opted into citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary` displays its
body as ordinary Markdown prose, with the same left alignment as the
surrounding prose and no opening citation badge or enclosing border.

A small marker in the right gutter identifies the passage's citation-checking
annotations. It does not claim that recorded evidence is current or accepted.
The outermost eligible citation fence has one marker; nested commentary
belongs to its list rather than displaying another marker.

Activating the marker opens the list of resolved citations from the source
passage, including its opening citation, citation-only metadata paragraphs,
and citations within nested commentary. Citations belonging to nested
requirement or example declarations are excluded. Repeated citations appear
once. Project citations link to their declarations; built-in citations retain
their descriptive hover text. The marker is keyboard operable, has an
accessible label, and shows visible keyboard focus. Opening the list does not
hide the passage. Inline citations within explanatory prose retain their
usual rendering.

Rendering does not change the source passage, its discovered references, or
its review inputs. Unfenced citations, citations inside requirement or example
declarations, and utility-only commentary retain their existing rendering.
rationale:
I reviewed the two supplied tests in `src/lib.rs` and found no adequacy gap. I did not request implementation source. **Main test:** `reviewed_passages_show_one_gutter_list_and_preserve_prose_and_literal_contexts` builds a chapter with many cases and checks the rendered output for each obligation in `requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary.display`. - **Ordinary prose, no opening badge or border:** - The fenced body renders as plain paragraphs. The test parses the output with pulldown_cmark and asserts `

The ordinary paragraph…` and `

Nested prose.

`. - The prose after `` contains no `alt="cite rules.other"`, and only one `rules.ready` badge, the explicit inline one, so no opening badge is repeated. - The test reads the `.habeas-citation-passage` CSS rule. It asserts `padding: 0`, `border: 0`, a left margin of `0` after parsing the margin shorthand, and `position: relative`. - **One marker, with nested commentary folded into the list:** - The test asserts exactly one `habeas-citation-passage` and one `habeas-citation-list`, even though a nested `::::{cite}` fence is present. - The marker CSS has `position: absolute` and `right:` but no `left:`. The panel CSS has `max-width` and absolute positioning. - **List contents:** - There are exactly 4 `
  • ` entries: the opening `habeas:util`, the metadata paragraph `rules.other`, the inline and nested `rules.ready`, and the definition's `rules.term_rule`. - Repeated citations appear once. `rules.ready` is cited inline and in a nested fence, and `list.matches(alt="cite rules.ready")` is asserted to be 1. - Citations inside the nested `req` and `example` declarations (`rules.inside`) are excluded from the list. - The test asserts that the declaration chapters `guide.nested` and `guide.sample` contain their own `rules.inside` badge. - A project citation links to its declaration (`href="rules.html#habeas-req-rules.other"`). The built-in citation keeps its hover text (`habeas-builtin" title=`). - **Accessibility and non-hiding:** - The summary has `aria-label="Show citations for this passage"` and a title. - It is a native `
    `/``, so it is keyboard operable. A `:focus-visible` outline rule is asserted. - The test asserts the prose follows `
    ` as a sibling, so opening the list does not hide the passage. - **Retained rendering:** - The unfenced outside citation keeps its badge and link. - Citations in `req`, `example` and `definition` declarations keep their existing rendering. - The utility-only fence keeps its `habeas-fenced-ref` rendering. - Literal code, inline code, escaped citations, unresolved fences, HTML-literal fences and unclosed fences are preserved verbatim. - **Source unchanged:** the test asserts the source file contents and `text_references` output are identical before and after rendering. **Supporting test:** `citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details` runs a table of container types (`req`, `example`, `definition`, `note`, `cite`, `impl`, `test`). - For a `:::{cite}` opening, the opening and metadata citations appear in the annotation block before the prose, and not in the visible prose. - The opening citation's badge appears exactly once, in the annotations. - Declarations still keep their full citation metadata, and the source and declarations are unchanged. The marker's static content (a title and a symbol) makes no claim about whether evidence is current or accepted. That needs no separate test. The exact left alignment and gutter placement are checked through CSS assertions rather than a browser render. This is a reasonable verification for this project, and I did not count it as a gap.

::::{req} citation_review.book_commentary
A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or
example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review.
A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation
other than `habeas:util`.
The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage. Its opening
citation and citations throughout its body belong to one review, including
citations inside nested commentary containers. References inside nested
requirement or example declarations belong to those declarations' assessments.
The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather
than the whole chapter. Its inputs include the passage and each cited
declaration or built-in text, with the terminology they use. For project
requirements and examples, the reviewer checks that the passage's claims agree
with and are supported by the cited declarations. Contradicting or unsupported
claims produce a negative assessment. Built-in citations retain their
permitted-role and stated-criteria checks under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection,
and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Their identities follow the existing outline-selector rules. Rendering follows
{cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. Unfenced book citations retain
their existing behavior.
